text: e. Suppose the government eliminates the ban on selling puppies. Policymakers instead focus on the positive externality from puppies: They bring joy to the neighbors even though the neighbors did not purchase the dog. Draw the marginal social benefit of puppies in a supply and demand figure, and label the deadweight loss attributable to the externality. Answer: See textbook Exhibit 9.5. The key here is at the market equilibrium, an additional puppy would deliver a larger marginal benefit to society than the marginal cost to puppy producers. So the market stopped providing puppies “too soon,” effectively leaving social surplus on the table. This is because, practically speaking, there is no way for producers to charge your neighbors for the joy they get from the puppy you buy.
